next_phase: Risk-first persisted seller journey, financial oracle and foreign-ID matrices; no autonomous production fixes.

resolved_findings.journey: Revise acquisition evidence and review contribution
resolved_findings.expected: A newer UNKNOWN revision of a cost key invalidates that key's older known amount for current contribution; historical as-of queries may retain the earlier evidence.
resolved_findings.actual: The January cost 200.01 is still used after a February UNKNOWN revision of the same key. The February summary reports contribution -103.04 and no missing inputs. _cost_evidence_rows filters UNKNOWN rows before choosing the latest version, resurrecting the superseded known row.
resolved_findings.business_impact: A seller can receive a qualified profit/loss estimate based on acquisition evidence they explicitly marked unknown.
resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Select the latest applicable cost revision first, then preserve UNKNOWN as a blocker; retain valid historical as-of behavior and cost lineage. Implement only with separate remediation authorization.

resolved_findings.journey: Retry a stock movement without duplicating or misacknowledging it
resolved_findings.expected: Identical retries return the original movement; conflicting delta or intent under the same key produces an explicit conflict rather than success for a different request.
resolved_findings.actual: After recording delta 1, reusing the same key with delta 99 returns HTTP 200 and the original balance. Duplicate lookup checks only item/key, not movement identity. No extra stock was added; the defect is silent acceptance of conflicting intent.
resolved_findings.business_impact: A seller or retrying client can believe a requested correction succeeded although a different earlier movement was returned.
resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Define canonical semantic replay identity and reject changed movement payloads while retaining identical retry and concurrency safety.

resolved_findings.journey: Record and safely retry sale/refund evidence
resolved_findings.expected: An existing source event ID must not acknowledge materially different monetary evidence as an identical replay.
resolved_findings.actual: Replaying the recorded sale with amount 999999 returns HTTP 201/idempotent true and the old event. Both preflight and uniqueness-recovery paths return the existing event without checking amount/type/reference identity. Existing data is not overwritten.
resolved_findings.business_impact: Conflicting sale or refund evidence can be silently discarded while a client sees a success response, obscuring reconciliation errors.
resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Compare normalized authoritative event identity in both replay paths and return a conflict for changed evidence, without weakening identical-delivery deduplication.

resolved_findings.journey: Acknowledge then resolve a signal with traceable HUMAN intent
resolved_findings.expected: A resolve request cannot reuse an acknowledge key and receive a successful response for the earlier transition.
resolved_findings.actual: A resolve request using the acknowledge key returns HTTP 200, the old transition ID and ACKNOWLEDGED state. _transition looks up owner/key but does not compare signal, target state or note.
resolved_findings.business_impact: The displayed/requested HUMAN intent and audit transition may disagree, making operational review unreliable.

evidence.name: Resolve acknowledged as the old transition

resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Validate semantic transition scope and target under the canonical owner/key lock; preserve identical concurrent replays.

resolved_findings.journey: Replenish stock and refresh operational guidance
resolved_findings.expected: A rescan after stock recovery must retire or explicitly stale the obsolete out-of-stock claim; acknowledgement alone does not make old evidence current.
resolved_findings.actual: After the same item is replenished from 0 to 20 and rescanned, its signal remains ACKNOWLEDGED/critical with evidence available 0, source version v1 and confidence 0.90. The scan upserts current matches but does not invalidate no-longer-matching signals.
resolved_findings.business_impact: A seller may waste time or make unnecessary replenishment decisions from a high-confidence obsolete recommendation. No automatic procurement was executed.
reproduction_steps: Inspect test_15_source_changes_rescan_and_signal_resolution and the preceding stock adjustment.

evidence.name: Old source claim after replenishment and rescan

resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile emitted fingerprints against current source state, retaining history while transitioning obsolete claims to a truthful noncurrent state. Do not auto-approve any business action.

resolved_findings.journey: Distinguish rehearsal data from real marketplace evidence
resolved_findings.expected: Financial fallback from fake-provider orders remains explicitly synthetic, even when no separate financial event exists.
resolved_findings.actual: The Flipkart summary contains only fake orders, canonical_order_fallback true and event_count 0, but synthetic_provider false. The flag inspects FinancialEvent source_type only and ignores fake order totals/provenance. The UI uses this flag to choose Synthetic fixture versus Canonical evidence.
resolved_findings.business_impact: A rehearsal can be presented as non-synthetic financial evidence, undermining trust in seller readiness and forecasts.

evidence.name: Fake-order fallback with false synthetic flag

resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Propagate synthetic/trust provenance through every contributing canonical source, never promote missing source classification to real/verified evidence.

resolved_findings.journey: Resolve and reopen persisted seller work
resolved_findings.expected: Selecting Resolved retrieves and displays persisted resolved signals with useful history.
resolved_findings.actual: After resolving a card, choosing Resolved shows no card although the detail API reports RESOLVED and history. The select updates ngModel only; load() requests include_resolved only when called later, so the current dataset excludes resolved rows. Reproduced on desktop/mobile.
resolved_findings.business_impact: Sellers cannot reliably find completed work through the offered status filter and may think their review history was lost.
reproduction_steps: QA-P3-04: acknowledge and resolve the browser warning, then choose Resolved without another refresh.

evidence.name: Browser screenshots, trace and API proof

resolved_findings.suggested_fix: Trigger an authoritative reload on the status change and keep loading/error/context feedback; do not remove the filter or relax the browser assertion.

browser_timing_correction.change: Only the QA-owned restart request gets timeout 45000 plus an explanatory comment. No assertion, locator, input or expected business behavior changed.
Only the QA-owned restart request gets timeout 45000 plus an explanatory comment. No assertion, locator, input or expected business behavior changed.

reviewed_findings.journey: Revise acquisition evidence and review contribution
reviewed_findings.expected: A newer UNKNOWN revision of a cost key invalidates that key's older known amount for current contribution; historical as-of queries may retain the earlier evidence.
reviewed_findings.actual: The January cost 200.01 is still used after a February UNKNOWN revision of the same key. The February summary reports contribution -103.04 and no missing inputs. _cost_evidence_rows filters UNKNOWN rows before choosing the latest version, resurrecting the superseded known row.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: A seller can receive a qualified profit/loss estimate based on acquisition evidence they explicitly marked unknown.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Select the latest applicable cost revision first, then preserve UNKNOWN as a blocker; retain valid historical as-of behavior and cost lineage. Implement only with separate remediation authorization.

reviewed_findings.journey: Retry a stock movement without duplicating or misacknowledging it
reviewed_findings.expected: Identical retries return the original movement; conflicting delta or intent under the same key produces an explicit conflict rather than success for a different request.
reviewed_findings.actual: After recording delta 1, reusing the same key with delta 99 returns HTTP 200 and the original balance. Duplicate lookup checks only item/key, not movement identity. No extra stock was added; the defect is silent acceptance of conflicting intent.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: A seller or retrying client can believe a requested correction succeeded although a different earlier movement was returned.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Define canonical semantic replay identity and reject changed movement payloads while retaining identical retry and concurrency safety.

reviewed_findings.journey: Record and safely retry sale/refund evidence
reviewed_findings.expected: An existing source event ID must not acknowledge materially different monetary evidence as an identical replay.
reviewed_findings.actual: Replaying the recorded sale with amount 999999 returns HTTP 201/idempotent true and the old event. Both preflight and uniqueness-recovery paths return the existing event without checking amount/type/reference identity. Existing data is not overwritten.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: Conflicting sale or refund evidence can be silently discarded while a client sees a success response, obscuring reconciliation errors.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Compare normalized authoritative event identity in both replay paths and return a conflict for changed evidence, without weakening identical-delivery deduplication.

reviewed_findings.journey: Acknowledge then resolve a signal with traceable HUMAN intent
reviewed_findings.expected: A resolve request cannot reuse an acknowledge key and receive a successful response for the earlier transition.
reviewed_findings.actual: A resolve request using the acknowledge key returns HTTP 200, the old transition ID and ACKNOWLEDGED state. _transition looks up owner/key but does not compare signal, target state or note.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: The displayed/requested HUMAN intent and audit transition may disagree, making operational review unreliable.

evidence.name: Resolve acknowledged as the old transition

reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Validate semantic transition scope and target under the canonical owner/key lock; preserve identical concurrent replays.

reviewed_findings.journey: Replenish stock and refresh operational guidance
reviewed_findings.expected: A rescan after stock recovery must retire or explicitly stale the obsolete out-of-stock claim; acknowledgement alone does not make old evidence current.
reviewed_findings.actual: After the same item is replenished from 0 to 20 and rescanned, its signal remains ACKNOWLEDGED/critical with evidence available 0, source version v1 and confidence 0.90. The scan upserts current matches but does not invalidate no-longer-matching signals.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: A seller may waste time or make unnecessary replenishment decisions from a high-confidence obsolete recommendation. No automatic procurement was executed.
reproduction_steps: Inspect test_15_source_changes_rescan_and_signal_resolution and the preceding stock adjustment.

evidence.name: Old source claim after replenishment and rescan

reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile emitted fingerprints against current source state, retaining history while transitioning obsolete claims to a truthful noncurrent state. Do not auto-approve any business action.

reviewed_findings.journey: Reopen the exact calculation used before a later refund or cost revision
reviewed_findings.expected: If historical calculation review is offered, earlier metrics and complete input lineage can be reconstructed; otherwise explicitly document that only current projections are supported.
reviewed_findings.actual: The supported authority overwrites one calculation row per scope/version. A later refund keeps the ID but changes metrics; the list is current projections, not immutable versions. Lineage lists event IDs but not the cost evidence used. This is a missing workflow, not a broken existing immutable-history contract. The final test validates the actual mutable contract.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: A seller cannot reconstruct the exact earlier profitability calculation from this projection alone, even though source events remain persisted.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Define whether retained calculation versions are required; reuse canonical snapshot/audit patterns and include applicable cost/source identities. Do not relabel current projections as immutable history.

reviewed_findings.journey: Turn an advisory signal into an explicitly reviewed supported action
reviewed_findings.expected: Distinguish signal acknowledgement from a durable canonical HUMAN approval; do not claim approval or execution where only an advisory response exists.
reviewed_findings.actual: The request-action authority returns approval_required and says the recommendation is recorded, but it adds no durable approval/action record. There is no approve/reject/failed-execution/retry lifecycle in this authority. The default-deny external boundary is working and was not bypassed.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: A first-time seller may mistake a requested or acknowledged signal for a saved authorization or completed action.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Clarify messaging and route only supported actions to their existing canonical HUMAN authorities; do not add a duplicate approval system or expose remote execution in QA.

reviewed_findings.journey: Create a first stock record from the inventory empty state
reviewed_findings.expected: An inventory empty state gives a supported UI path to create the canonical item before adjustments, reservations and channel mapping.
reviewed_findings.actual: The workspace tells the seller to create a product stock record, but exposes filters, adjustments, ledger and mapping only for existing items. Its canonical creation API exists; this suite seeds it through that API. Product master inventory fields are a separate model and are not a demonstrated replacement for this missing handoff.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: API fixtures can exercise populated inventory, but a first-time seller can still encounter a UI onboarding dead end.
reproduction_steps: Inspect the empty state and controls in unified-inventory.component.ts
Compare POST /api/v1/inventory/items with MarketplaceService UI callers.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Plan an explicit canonical creation/handoff using the existing API, with opening balance provenance and HUMAN review. Do not duplicate stock ledgers.

reviewed_findings.journey: Read due-diligence, economic and financial evidence on mobile
reviewed_findings.expected: Every relevant visible caption and table cell can be evaluated without claiming obscured or incomplete contrast checks as passes.
reviewed_findings.actual: All 107 original repeated-state target occurrences were examined after real scrolling using axe. 101 passed and six caption occurrences remain incomplete; no contrast violation was confirmed. A separate financial-loss screen also retains four incomplete mobile nodes. These are manual-review tasks, not confirmed WCAG failures and not resolved findings.
reviewed_findings.business_impact: Automated testing cannot yet establish readability of every mobile caption/obscured table element; first-time seller comprehension and assistive-technology behavior still need review.
reproduction_steps: Inspect QA-P3-06 scrolling diagnostics and QA-P3-03 full-document axe findings on mobile.
reviewed_findings.suggested_fix: Manually review clipped captions and table reading/keyboard behavior, then authorize a focused responsive/accessibility correction if needed. Retain full-document axe checks and do not suppress incomplete results.

gaps: Real provider, external publication, payment/refund dispatch, supplier contact and marketplace authorization are intentionally not executed.
Order creation/lifecycle uses the actual synthetic-provider API; the UI is a read-only projection, not a seller order-entry or refund-dispatch authority.

Action Center supports local signal acknowledge/snooze/resolve/reopen, not a complete persisted approval/rejection/execution workflow. Its request-action response is not proof of an executed or durably approved action.
Independent fresh-process database reconstruction is tested; database service outage and publishing-worker restart remain NOT EXECUTED to avoid interacting with unrelated runtime/backup services.
Browser failures/timeouts and committed-response loss use explicit network interception, not a claim of real infrastructure failure or worker recovery.
ORM metadata fixtures do not validate the complete migration chain. No migration certification is claimed.
No applicable GST treatment, real marketplace fee schedule, bank reconciliation or complete net-profit accounting is inferred from hypothetical synthetic evidence.
Keyboard checks are bounded; screen-reader/assistive-technology certification and comprehensive modal focus-trap testing remain unexecuted.
